units.title: Locate the tooth tissues
units.lesson: Enamel covers the anatomical crown; dentin forms much of the tooth beneath enamel and around the pulp space. The pulp is internal soft tissue. Location helps distinguish a tooth’s hard tissues from its neurovascular contents. These are structural relationships, not a depth-based diagnosis or a treatment rule.
units.question: Which tissue lies beneath enamel around the pulp space?
units.explanation: Dentin surrounds the internal pulp space beneath enamel.
rationales: This is the tooth hard tissue described.

units.title: Know what pulp contains
units.lesson: The dental pulp contains nerves, blood vessels and connective tissue. It is not an empty canal. Its role in tooth development and its relationship with surrounding dentin explain why pulp biology matters in endodontics. Pain alone does not provide every detail about pulp condition; this foundation does not assign a clinical diagnosis.
units.question: Which description fits normal dental pulp?
choices: Soft connective tissue with vessels and nerves
units.explanation: Pulp is living soft tissue containing vessels and nerves.
rationales: The pulp space is normally occupied by tissue.

units.title: Follow the caries mechanism
units.lesson: Plaque bacteria can metabolize dietary sugars and starches and produce acids. Repeated acid exposure can shift the tooth surface toward mineral loss. Early mineral changes are not the same thing as an established hole. Think in terms of a disease process and mineral balance, rather than treating every change in colour as proof of cavitation.
units.question: Which process directly contributes to enamel mineral loss in caries?
units.explanation: Acid generated by cariogenic bacteria can drive mineral loss.
rationales: This links biofilm activity and mineral change.
Pulp formation is a developmental process.

units.title: Classify restoration by how it is made
units.lesson: A direct restoration is placed in the tooth without fabrication as a separate laboratory restoration. ADA groups direct materials into amalgam, resin-based composite, glass ionomer and resin-modified glass ionomer. Classification describes the material and method; it is not a universal recommendation for a particular lesion. Material selection needs more context than a family name.
units.question: What defines a direct restoration in this classification?
choices: It is placed directly in the tooth
It must be a laboratory-made bridge
units.explanation: Direct describes placement without separate laboratory fabrication.
rationales: A bridge is a different restoration category.

choices: Every colour change proves an established cavity
The pulp is replaced by enamel
units.explanation: Repeated acid challenges can favour net demineralization without proving cavitation from colour alone.
rationales: Surface colour does not establish a hole.
